 Judgment

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 02.04.2024 at about 12.30 (00-30) am.

2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 02.04.2024 at about 12.30 (00-30)am, infront of Varthur Bridge Road,
Varthur-Varthur Kodi Road, Bengaluru city, at that time of accident the petitioner was riding Bajaj Paltinum motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-JW-6154 along with pillion rider with carefully, observing all traffic rules and regulations.
At that time Ashok L e y l a n d T i p p e r L o r r y b e a r i n g N o . T N - 7 0 - T C - 2 8 6 ( C H A R S I N o .

MB1JJVLD6RRPS9750 & ENGINE No.RPEZ700005) came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated and underwent surgery and after better and expert treatment he was discharged with an advise for follow up treatment.
So far he has spent huge amount towards his treatment, nourishment, food etc., Due to the said accidental injuries, suffering from permanent disability.
The injuries caused in the accident are permanent in nature.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, working as coolie and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.

The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Ashok Leyland Tipper Lorry bearing Registration No.TN-70- TC-286 and Whitefield Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the Lorry in Cr.No.0059/2024 p/u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant compensation as prayed in the petition.
4. In response to the notice, the respondent Nos.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this court hence, place ex-parte.

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent in its written statement has denied the entire petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the 1 st respondent in respect of the the Tipper Lorry bearing No.TN-70-TC-286.
Further stated that the driver of the lorry did not possess a valid Driving license at the time of accident.
Further denied the involvement of the Lorry in the accident.
Further the offending vehicle did not possess a valid FC and Permit as on the date of accident.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further denied the age, occupation, medical expenses etc., Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant.
Accordingly, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-70-TC- 286 by its driver in RTA took place on 02.04.2024 at about 12.30am on Varthur-Varthur Kodi Road,
Varthur Bridge Road, Bangalore?
Issue No.2: Whether the petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
Issue No.3: What Order or Award?
6. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked 12 documents as Exs.P1 to P12.
He has also got examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.13 to 15.
The respondent No.2 did not examine any witness on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments canvassed by the learned counsel for the parties.

8. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above points are as follows:
Issue No.1 :In the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No3: As per final order, for the foregoing:
#REASONS#
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Twelve documents as Exs.P1 to P12.
He has also got examined Dr.Chidnand K.J.C as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.13 to 15.
The respondent No.2 did not examine any witness on its behalf.
The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
10. It is the specific case of the respondent No.2 that the driver of the offending lorry was not holding a valid driving license as on the date of accident.

They have denied the mode of accident as Dileep Das vs Ashok Leyland Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76612190/
3 explained by the petitioner.

sentences.text: To prove the same it has not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
11. The petitioner has reiterated the petition averments in the chief examination.
He has subjected to cross examination.
In the cross examination he has deposed that, himself lodged the complaint, the pillion rider was Ubber Customer.
He had not noticed whether the offending vehicle with goods or empty.
He admitted that, vehicle movements are very high in Varthur Road.
He admitted that, the accident spot was straight road.
He has not noticed that on his left side vehicle were not allowed.
He admitted himself and offending vehicle are moving in same path and they intent to take turn which was ahead of them.
He further denied other suggestions of the respondents counsel.
12. Before evaluating the evidence of the PW.1, for cost of repetition, it is necessary to reproduce the case of the petitioner.

That On 02.04.2024 at about 12.30 (00-30)am, infront of Varthur Bridge Road, Varthur-Varthur Kodi Road, Bangalore city, at that time of accident the petitioner was riding Bajaj Paltinum motorcycle bearing No.KA- 01-JW-6154 along with pillion rider with carefully,
observing all traffic rules and regulations.

At that time Ashok Leyland Tipper Lorry bearing No.TN-70- TC-286 (CHARSI N.MB1JJVLD6RRPS9750 & ENGINE No.RPEZ700005) came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle.
As a result both have fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

13. It is worth note herein that the police materials are clearly depicts that, the petitioner was riding his motorcycle along with pillion rider, both wearing helmet proceeding from Varthur Kodi Main Road, Varthur towards Varthur Kodi i.e., from West direction towards North direction, at that time the offending Ashok Leyland Lorry came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to impact, petitioner and pillion rider were fell down and the Lorry ran over the pillion rider, she succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
14. The MV report at Ex.P.5 shows that the offending Lorry bearing No.TN-70-TC-286 got damages to its (1) Front bumper at right side.

Similarly petitioner's motorcycle also got damaged to its (1)
Front right side head lamp mask and rear view mirror damaged, (2) Front right side foot rest and crash guard damaged and (3) Rear tail lamp assembly damaged.
By considering these damages it can be hold that the Lorry has dashed to rear side of the motorcycle and caused the accident.

It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.
15.
The spot sketch is also clearly demonstrated that the offending vehicle and petitioner were proceeding same lane and the accident was occurred at the circle.

Thus, In overall consideration of these documents coupled with the evidence of PW-1, it would clearly establish that the accident in question had occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-70-TC-286.
Therefore, I hold that the accident is caused due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN- 70-TC-286.

The Court cannot adopt strict Dileep Das vs Ashok Leyland Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76612190/
4 liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the respondent vehicle.

sentences.text: But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
Therefore, a straight jacket formula cannot be adopted in accepting the rash and negligence on the part of driver of the insured.
So, the materials on record clearly indicates that the accident has occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.2: the claimant has produced Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.3.

It shows that the claimant has sustained swelling right lower limb elbow knee, tenderness deformity, bleeds (Bullae)
prevent distal put of stretch put up medial aspect leg which are grievous in nature.
X-ray shows HBB Right leg, right medial malleolus.
17. In this regard, the petitioner has got examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW.2.

The PW.2 has stated in the chief examination affidavit paragraph Nos.1 to 5 that petitioner has sustained "right both bone leg fracture with right medial malleoli fracture with compartmental syndrome.
He took treatment in form of fasciotomy with EX fix and later admitted for definitive management in the form of CRIF with IMIL nailing..

Further PW.2 has noted at the time of assessing disability that the range of movements of knee and ankle restricted, quadriceps wasting is seen, healed surgical scar over knee, associated with pain on movements knee and ankle, Daily activities cross leg sitting,
squatting for using Indian toilets were found to be difficulty in limb.
X- ray shows fracture united with implant in situ.
The PW.2 has opined that the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability for limb is 51% and to the whole body at 17%.
17A. The PW.2 has been subjected to cross examination.
During the cross examination, PW.2 has stated that he has given treatment to the petitioner along with other Doctors team.
The petitioner has come 2 to 3 times for further treatment.
The fractures are united.
The operation done to the tibia only.
There is no loss of muscle.
He has denied the further suggestions of the counsel for the other side.
18. Before discussing on this point, it is necessary to advert to the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, "the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The Court or Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
1 2011 ACJ 1 A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned".

sentences.text: Our Hon'ble High Court has held in a case MFA.811 OF 2015 (MV-I) decided on 18 July, 2019 in between Rajanna @ Raju and another V/s Srinivas and another that "It is necessary to understand the meaning of the expression "permanent disability", which has been elucidated in Rajkumar.

entities.text: Rajanna @ Raju and another V/s Srinivas and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the Hon'ble Supreme Court, disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for a human being.

Permanent disability refers to the residuary incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation, after achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured.
Temporary disability refers to the incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body on account of the injury, which will cease to exist at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation.
Permanent disability can be either partial or total.

Partial permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform all the duties and bodily functions that he could perform before the accident, though he is able to perform some of them and is still able to engage in some gainful activity.
Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.

The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor accidents injuries, are of a much wider range when compared to the physical disabilities which are enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 ("the Disabilities Act",
for short).

entities.text: Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: But if any of the disabilities enumerated in Section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.

12. Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and, if so,
the extent of such permanent disability.

By considering the dictums of Hon'ble Supreme Court and Our Hon'ble High Court and also evidence led by the medical officer, It is appears to Court that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
And it certainly affected on his functional capacity.
The petition discloses that the petitioner was working as coolie and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.

. The evidence of the medical officer clearly clinches that on clinical examination, the medical officer has pointed out the difficulties of the injured person to do routine work with some difficulties.
It means, the petitioner is not in position to do the earlier work effectively.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held in a ALIVELI MALLAREDDY Vs 2 CIVIL APPEAL NO. OF 2025(Arising out of SLP (C) No. 19636 of 2024) SURTHANI LINGANNA @ CHINNA LINGANNA & Others.

sentences.text: By considering the age, nature of injuries and treatment, it is appears to Court that the petitioner has suffered functional disability 10.2% (51%  1/5 for right lower limb) to the whole body.

As such,
the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 10.2% whole body.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

PECUNIARY DAMAGES I. Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines,
transportation, nourishing food and misc. expenditures.
21.

The claimant has contended that he has taken treatment at Sanjaygandhi Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated and underwent surgery and after better and expert treatment he was discharged dated 07.04.2025 with an advise for follow up treatment.
The documents placed by the petitioner indicates that he has taken treatment before the said hospital from 02.04.2024 to 20.04.2024
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12.
On verification of the medical bills, there no repeated bills but includes advance bills.
Hence, I award a sum of Rs.67,346=00 as compensation to the claimant under the head of treatment and medical expenses.
As supra said, the petitioner has admitted in the said Hospital as an inpatient.
But he has furnished the Discharge Summary.
Considering the wound certificate and chief examination information that the petitioner was admitted in the above said hospital from 02.04.2024 to 20.04.2024 and 04.06.2024 for total 19 days.
Hence, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.500/-per day for attendant and Rs.1500/- for food and nourishment charges, which would comes Rs.38,000/-.
A sum of Rs.38,000=00 is awarded under the head of attendant, food and nourishment charges.
(ii) LOSS OF EARNING 22.

The claimant has contended that, he was working as coolie and earning sum of Rs.25,000/-
per month.
In this regard, the petitioner has not produced any documents nor examined any witness.
He has failed to prove his exact income.
So, considering the nature of work notional income of Rs.16,500/-pm. is calculated to award loss of earning, it would meets the ends of justice.
Therefore, I award Rs.10,450=00 to the claimant under the head of loss of earning during the treatment.

(b) LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
23.
The claimant has examined the Doctor to substantiate the disability as PW-2.
As already discussed above, the petitioner was suffered disability.
The medical officer has given physical disability of 51% Points for functional loss of malocclusion.
By considering the nature of injuries and treatment, it is appears to Court that the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 10.2%.
As per the petition averments, the age of the claimant is 33 years.
The Aadhar Cardmarked at Exs.P11 and medical documents are clearly discloses that, the age of the petitioner was 33 years.

sentences.text: Therefore, the age of the claimant is considered as 33 years to assess the loss of future earning and the multiplier is 16.

As I have already stated the notional income of the claimant is Rs.16,500/-pm,
The loss of future earning is calculated as Rs.16,500/- (Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 16 (multiplier) X 10.2 (disability) 100 =Rs.3,23,136=00 which is the just and proper compensation payable to claimant.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES (GENERAL DAMAGES)
(iii) Damages for pain and suffering and trauma consequence of the injuries.
24.
The claimant has undergone pain and suffering during the accident and during the rehabilitation period.
Therefore, I award Rs.1,00,000/- as compensation to the claimant under the head of pain and suffering.
25. As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner require surgery for removal of implants.
In this regard neither the petitioner nor PW.2 has produced any estimation bill about further surgery.

As per the evidence of Pws.1 & 2 and looking at the earlier treatment cost and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under the head of Future Medical Expenses.

26. The claimant in all entitled for just compensation under the following heads:
Sl. NATURE OF THE HEADS COMPENSATION No. 01 Medical Expenses Rs.67,346=00 02 Loss of income during Rs.10,450=00 treatment 03

Attendant,
Food & Rs.38,000=00 Nourishment charges 04 Pain and Suffering Rs.1,00,000=00 05 Loss of future earning on Rs.3,23,136=00 account of disability 06
Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000=00 TOTAL Rs.5,58,932=00 27.
The next question is the liability to pay the said compensation.
As I discussed in supra, the accident was occurred sole negligence of offending vehicle's driver.
The petitioner proved that as on the date of accident the policy was in force.
Therefore, Respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1 and liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.2.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part.

The respondent No.2 is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.5,58,932=00 (Rupees Five Lakhs Fifty Eight Thousands Nine Hundred and Thirty Two Only) together interest @ 6% P.A (Except on future medical expenses) from the Dileep Das vs Ashok Leyland Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76612190/

The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor accidents injuries, are of a much wider range when compared to the physical disabilities which are enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 ("the Disabilities Act",
for short).
But if any of the disabilities enumerated in Section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.
